title: Big-four Australian bank workforce signals
subtitle: LinkedIn snapshot joined to APRA, ABS, and TEQSA public data. Aggregate rates only.
caveat: LinkedIn coverage is incomplete and biased toward people who maintain public profiles. These are relative market signals, not staff census figures. Cells with n < 30 are treated as sparse. Binomial shares use Wilson 95% intervals where shown.

method.wilson: 95% Wilson score intervals for binomial shares
method.sparse_rule: cells with n < 30 treated as sparse
method.score: 0–100 from coverage (40), median cell size (35), non-sparse share (25)

ranking.title: Stakeholder decision products
notes: Decision products only emit claims with n ≥ 30 and, where relevant, Wilson intervals.
This layer inherits bias from LinkedIn coverage; wording stays relative.

ranking.title: Function mix and org design proxies
notes: Technology/risk/markets shares use titled profiles only; unknown titles excluded.
Wilson 95% intervals reported for bank-level technology shares.
About-section coverage is only 44% — text clustering is not used for claims.
Certifications remain too sparse for leading indicators.

ranking.title: APRA / ABS public overlays
notes: LinkedIn density ≠ staff census; ABS and APRA denominators are official.
Profiles-per-branch mixes a biased numerator with an administrative denominator.
Best used for relative ranks across banks/states, not absolute labour-market shares.
APRA branch counts by SA3 for latest year (Table 1).

ranking.title: Employer transition network
notes: Edges require a prior employer in the experience history; many profiles lack usable sequences.
External company names are free text and may duplicate (Deloitte / Deloitte Australia).
Inter-bank cells are generally large enough for directional claims.

ranking.title: Career paths and CBA attractors
notes: Uses dated experience rows only; undated careers are excluded.
Function tags are regex heuristics on titles, so misclassification noise remains.
Cells with n < 30 are flagged as sparse.

headline_defensible.claim: Largest observed inbound competitor flow to CBA includes Westpac→CBA (577 moves).
VIC shows the highest big-four LinkedIn density vs ABS finance employment (21.6%).
